supports.excerpt:
6.5   References and further reading
            Chapter 7 develops the computational aspects of vector space scoring. Luhn
            (1957; 1958) describes some of the earliest reported applications of term weight-
            ing. His paper dwells on the importance of medium frequency terms (terms
            that are neither too commonplace nor too rare) and may be thought of as an-
            ticipating tf-idf and related weighting schemes. Spärck Jones (1972) builds
            on this intuition through detailed experiments showing the use of inverse
            document frequency in term weighting. A series of extensions and theoret-
            ical justifications of idf are due to Salton and Buckley (1987) Robertson and
            Jones (1976), Croft and Harper (1979) and Papineni (2001). Robertson main-
            tains a web page (http://www.soi.city.ac.uk/˜ser/idf.html) containing the history
            of idf, including soft copies of early papers that predated electronic versions
            of journal article. Singhal et al. (1996a) develop pivoted document length
            normalization. Probabilistic language models (Chapter 11) develop weight-
            ing techniques that are more nuanced than tf-idf; the reader will find this
            development in Section 11.4.3.
               We observed that by assigning a weight for each term in a document, a
            document may be viewed as a vector of term weights, one for each term in
            the collection. The SMART information retrieval system at Cornell (Salton
            1971b) due to Salton and colleagues was perhaps the first to view a doc-
            ument as a vector of weights. The basic computation of cosine scores as
            described in Section 6.3.3 is due to Zobel and Moffat (2006). The two query
            evaluation strategies term-at-a-time and document-at-a-time are discussed
            by Turtle and Flood (1995).
               The SMART notation for tf-idf term weighting schemes in Figure 6.15 is
            presented in (Salton and Buckley 1988, Singhal et al. 1995; 1996b). Not all
            versions of the notation are consistent; we most closely follow (Singhal et al.
            1996b). A more detailed and exhaustive notation was developed in Moffat
            and Zobel (1998), considering a larger palette of schemes for term and doc-
            ument frequency weighting. Beyond the notation, Moffat and Zobel (1998)
            sought to set up a space of feasible weighting functions through which hill-
            climbing approaches could be used to begin with weighting schemes that
            performed well, then make local improvements to identify the best combi-
            nations. However, they report that such hill-climbing methods failed to lead
            to any conclusions on the best weighting schemes.

skill_drafts.name: TF-IDF Term Weighting Reference
skill_drafts.description: Historical and theoretical foundation for term frequency-inverse document frequency weighting schemes in information retrieval. Documents the conceptual lineage and key citations from Luhn (1957) through modern probabilistic language models, enabling practitioners to understand and justify tf-idf variant selection.
contraindications: real-time query execution or immediate scoring computation needed
operational deployment requiring only implementation code
time-critical retrieval tasks where reference lookup is infeasible
triggers: implementing or understanding tf-idf variants, reviewing term weighting history, or justifying weighting scheme selection
constraints: This is reference material only; does not provide executable weighting algorithms.
Citations are historical; some early papers may require archival access.
output_contract: Practitioner can cite foundational papers (Luhn 1957, Spärck Jones 1972, Salton & Buckley 1987) and articulate the rationale for inverse document frequency and tf-idf weighting scheme selection.

metadata.prompt: When implementing or reviewing term weighting schemes, consult this reference to trace the intellectual history of tf-idf. Key foundational works: Luhn (1957, 1958) on medium-frequency term importance; Spärck Jones (1972) on inverse document frequency; Salton & Buckley (1987) on theoretical justifications; Robertson & Jones (1976), Croft & Harper (1979), Papineni (2001) on idf extensions; Singhal et al. (1996a) on pivoted document length normalization. The SMART system (Salton 1971b) pioneered vector representation of documents. Zobel & Moffat (2006) formalized cosine scoring. Moffat & Zobel (1998) developed exhaustive notation for weighting function spaces.

skill_drafts.name: Vector Space Document Representation
skill_drafts.description: Conceptual framework for representing documents as vectors of term weights and computing similarity scores using cosine distance. Covers the document-as-vector model, query vectorization, and dot-product scoring methodology.
applicable_signals: Designing or explaining document ranking systems
Training teams on vector space model foundations
Establishing baseline scoring methodology before advanced techniques
contraindications: Probabilistic language models are the primary scoring approach
Neural embedding methods are being used instead of classical vector space
Context requires modern deep learning-based retrieval systems
triggers: designing or explaining document ranking systems, implementing cosine similarity scoring, or training teams on vector space model foundations
constraints: This is a reference-level knowledge asset; it provides conceptual understanding, not operational code or parameter tuning
Assumes familiarity with basic linear algebra and document indexing concepts
output_contract: Practitioner understands document vectorization, query vectorization, and cosine score computation; can cite SMART system (Salton 1971) and Zobel & Moffat (2006); can explain why medium-frequency terms are important and how term weighting relates to tf-idf

metadata.prompt: Explain how documents are represented as vectors of term weights in the vector space model. Describe the process of vectorizing both documents and queries, and how cosine similarity is computed between them. Reference the SMART system (Salton 1971) as a foundational implementation and Zobel & Moffat (2006) for cosine score computation details.
